RustyNES **v2.3.9 "Crucible"** is not a feature release. A crucible is where something is tested to destruction rather than inspected, and that is what this release does to the project's own gates: what they cover, what they only appear to cover, and where a regression could still reach `main` unchallenged.

The v2.3.x line added five tools in four releases, and the recurring finding across all of them was never that the emulation was wrong. It was that **a check reported a pass it had not earned.** This release went looking for the rest of them.

**The accuracy contract is verified, not asserted.** `rustynes-apu` and `rustynes-core` both change here, so AccuracyCoin was re-run rather than reasoned about — and re-run *again* after the second round of deletions rather than only after the first: **141/141 (100.00%)** on the authoritative RAM decoder, nestest 0-diff.

## The docs-only CI skip had never worked

`dorny/paths-filter`'s `predicate-quantifier` defaults to `some`, which includes a file if it matches **any** pattern. The `code` filter is `'**'` followed by seven exclusions — so `'**'` matched everything and every `!` line under it was dead from the day it was written.

Proven from a run rather than the docs. A PR changing exactly one file logged:

```text
[modified] AGENTS.md
Filter code = true
Matching files: AGENTS.md [modified]
```

A markdown file matching a filter whose entire purpose is excluding markdown. Every documentation PR in the project's history had been running the full matrix — and that stopped being merely wasteful the day two docs-only PRs were *blocked* by an ARM cross-compile failure on jobs that should never have been scheduled.

Fixed with two filter steps, because `predicate-quantifier` is step-level and the two filters need opposite settings: `code` needs `every`, while `accuracy` is a list of **alternatives** and would become unsatisfiable under it — silently disabling the accuracy battery while fixing a different gate. Both directions are now observed on real PRs: `code = false` for a markdown-only change, and `code = true` listing *only* the `.rs` file when one joins a docs diff.

## The accuracy battery now runs at review time

`test-roms` was full-run only, so a regression landed on `main` rather than on the PR that caused it. It is now also triggered by a path filter covering the chip crates, the core, `rustynes-gamedb`, the harness and `tests/` — measured first: 11 of the last 40 merged PRs touch those paths, so ~72% still pay nothing.

`rustynes-gamedb` is in the list for a non-obvious reason: it rewrites the iNES header on load, so it changes what the emulator **is** before a cycle runs.

## Bounds calibrated against measurements, not claims

The ARM provisioning step failed on three consecutive PRs, and the log contained no apt error at all — only two `update` timeouts at exactly the bound, and an install killed mid-download. The bound came from a comment asserting "a healthy `update` on these runners is a few seconds", which had never been measured.

The log then gave the real number: **`Fetched 4201 kB in 4min 45s (14.7 kB/s)`**. Three orders of magnitude below normal — which is why the previous ~40 MB package set was *hopeless* rather than unlucky, needing roughly 45 minutes. No timeout could have saved it.

The step was also installing the wrong thing, and the comment above it said so without drawing the conclusion: it named `libc6-dev-arm64-cross` as the package that lands the headers, and stated the cross linker is unused because the gate is `cargo check` only. It was installing a whole cross toolchain — 20+ packages, one of them 21.1 MB — to obtain a dependency it had already identified. bindgen runs the *host* clang against `--sysroot` and never invokes the cross compiler.

## A freeze from one cartridge kept writing into the next

Not a stale label — an active, per-frame write into the wrong game. Both memory panels' freezes feed the app's raw-cheat overlay, applied after every frame, and neither was registered with the ROM-transition hook. A byte frozen while playing one game went on being written into the next at an address that means something else there.

The sweep that found it now covers every panel, under one rule: **derived output is discarded, user-authored input is kept, and only input that actively *writes* is neutralised.** So RAM Search baselines and reconstructed call stacks are cleared; watch lists and breakpoints survive, and breakpoints stay *armed*, because a breakpoint halts (visible, recoverable) where a freeze writes (silent, continuous).

Two negatives are recorded too, because they cost time to establish: the header editor **looks** ROM-bound and is not — it is a standalone file tool — and the event panel, trace status and HD-pixel coordinates are per-frame state or preferences.

## The config file is written atomically and durably

`fs::write` truncates then writes, so an interruption left the user holding a truncated `config.toml` — every keybinding, palette, shader preset and per-game setting. That window stopped being theoretical when saves became automatic: closing a ROM, moving a mixer slider, and finishing a Latency Oracle measurement all save without being asked.

Seven properties, and **five of them came from review rather than the first draft** — which is the honest summary of how this one went:

| property | why |
| --- | --- |
| sibling scratch file | across a filesystem boundary `rename` is not a rename |
| `fsync` before rename | `fs::write` returns at the page cache; an atomic rename over unsynced data is not durable |
| parent-directory sync | on POSIX the entry `rename` creates is itself a cache update |
| `create_new(true)` | `File::create` follows symlinks and truncates (CWE-377) |
| mode applied at creation | closes a window where the file sat at the umask default |
| symlink resolution | `fs::write` follows a link; `rename` replaces it — including a **broken** link, the freshly-created dotfiles case |
| pid + per-call counter | and it is what makes exclusive creation adoptable at all |

## Two shipped features told the truth for the first time

**Movies record two ports.** `FrameInput` models P1 and P2, so a recording made with the Four Score adapter captures half of what drove the run — while the Replay panel printed "Four Score (P1..P4)" at the moment a user decides to press Record. Widening the format is a `.rnm` epoch change, so this is disclosed at three levels rather than papered over, with the caveat printed directly under the claim it qualifies.

**A Latency Oracle measurement is remembered per game**, and a failed save now says so instead of being swallowed. Remembering is still not applying: nothing here touches `run_ahead`, and an inconclusive result is not remembered at all.

## Under the surface

- **A real produce-to-visible latency series.** The end-to-end figure needed a per-sample total, because `p95(A) + p95(B)` is not `p95(A + B)` — the same invalid arithmetic this project retracted a published table for, in the addition direction.
- **The two-acquisition lock race is measured rather than reasoned about**, with both a hit count and a denominator, because "the race did not fire" and "nothing was observed" are different facts.
- **A RAM Atlas address can leave the panel** into RAM Watch, carrying its verdict *and the lens that produced it* — liveness is relative to the observable, and the watch list is where an unqualified "LIVE" would outlive the panel that qualified it.
- **257 lines of dead code removed** — an APU pair (34), a closed `LockstepBus` DMA-service island (183), and `drain_dma` (40), a function called on every CPU read, every CPU write and every bus cycle whose entire body was `let _ = read_addr;` and whose comments claimed the legacy service below it "stays active for the default build". Alongside them, **25 of 29 `#[allow(dead_code)]` attributes were suppressing nothing** — established by stripping them and re-running clippy across all eight gated combinations, because an item can be live by default and dead on wasm, which is precisely the case that would have earned the attribute.
- **The SAFETY-comment rule is now a gate.** All 91 unsafe sites already carried a justification; two had it where a human reads correctly and a checker cannot. `clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks` is enabled, and demonstrated to fail.
- **Two `cargo deny` advisory ignores retired** — their own entry said to remove them once the resolve moved past quick-xml 0.40, and it had.
